synopsis: University of Michigan researchers learned naturalistic driving distributions, generated more critical interactions in simulation, and used importance sampling to recover unbiased estimates for the modelled event class [f631, f1295]. The corpus reports orders-of-magnitude acceleration in on-road lane-change and car-following evaluations during 2016–2017, with 2016 factors of roughly 300–100,000 for car-following crashes and 2,000–20,000 for lane-change conflicts [f632, f1220, f1221]. These are proofs of principle for on-road automated-driving behavior, not evidence about sensor performance in adverse conditions or off-road perception failures such as quarry-wall radar multipath, occlusion and sensor-position variation [f1298, f1222, f1301]. For planning, the accelerated evaluations do not eliminate model validation or sensor and vehicle tests, and no regulator accepted a production AEB on their basis [f1299, f1300].

relations.note: Both describe increasing rare-event frequency and statistically reweighting outcomes using importance sampling.
